# Multiphase chemical equilibrium {#sec-ch05}

`EquilibriumTP` finds the composition at which a set of reactions is at chemical equilibrium, at a given temperature
and pressure. The species may sit in several phases: one ideal gas and any number of condensed phases, each an ideal
mixture. The caller gives the equilibrium constants as $\ln K^\circ_r$, either its own or from the bundled NASA-9 data.
The solver writes one condition per reaction in logarithms of activities (@sec-ch05-conditions). It moves the
composition only along the reactions, so every element is conserved by construction, and solves the conditions by a
bounded Newton iteration in the reaction extents (@sec-ch05-newton). It reports a status, an iteration count and the
remaining error per cell instead of raising (@sec-ch05-diagnostics). The options come from a YAML file or from the
API (@sec-ch05-options), and the constants from `Nasa9LogK` (@sec-ch05-log-k). @fig-ch05-dependency-map shows how the
schemes depend on each other.

: Schemes of this chapter. {#tbl-ch05-schemes}

**Relation to the other solvers.** The saturation adjustment of @sec-ch04 and this solver both look for an
equilibrium at fixed $T$ and $p$, but they answer different questions, and neither calls the other:

| | saturation adjustment (@sec-ch04) | log-K solver (this chapter) |
|---|---|---|
| reactions | condensation (`type: nucleation`) | any balanced set (`type: equilibrium`) |
| constants | saturation curves $K_r(T)$ in Pa$^{m}$ | $\ln K^\circ_r$ supplied by the caller, dimensionless |
| condensed phases | pure, unit activity | ideal mixtures; a one-species phase has unit activity |
| a phase may vanish | yes: complementarity, @eq-ch04-conditions-saturation | no: every amount stays above `mole-floor` |
| state | mole fractions or concentrations, also fixed $U$, $V$ | amounts in mol, fixed $T$, $p$ only |
| used by | `ThermoX`, `ThermoY` | the caller only |

: The two equilibrium solvers. {#tbl-ch05-relation}

The kinetics of @sec-ch06 relax a composition towards equilibrium in time. Its reverse rate constants use the forward
rate constant divided by an equilibrium constant built from NASA-9 Gibbs energies by the same function,
`nasa9_gibbs_RT`, in concentration units
(`KineticsImpl::forward_with_rate_constants`,
{{< code src/kinetics/kinetics.cpp KineticsImpl::forward_with_rate_constants >}}). A reversible gas-phase network
that reaches a steady state therefore meets the gas-phase form of @eq-ch05-conditions-residual, with the same
constants when the two read the same NASA-9 coefficients. No code in kintera checks that the two agree.

## Equilibrium conditions in logarithmic form, with element balance and several phases {#sec-ch05-conditions}

### Summary

Each reaction is at equilibrium when the sum of its species' log-activities, weighted by the stoichiometric
coefficients, equals $\ln K^\circ_r$. A species' activity is its mole fraction within its own phase, and for the gas
also the pressure over the standard pressure. So a species in a one-species condensed phase has unit activity, and
species in a condensed mixture follow Raoult's law. The solver does not track elements. It changes the amounts only
along the reactions, which conserves every element whenever each reaction is balanced. Unlike the saturation conditions
of @sec-ch04-conditions, these are equalities for every reaction: a phase that should be absent at equilibrium cannot
satisfy them.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** The conditions every log-K solve aims for, @eq-ch05-conditions-residual.

**Data.** Amounts [mol], phase of each species, $T$ [K], $p$ [Pa], $\ln K^\circ_r$ [-].

**Placement.** Inside `phase_equilibrate_tp`, per cell.

**Activation.** Every reaction of the options, always.

**Guarantee / limits.** Elements conserved by construction; ideal mixtures; no phase can vanish.

**Evidence.** See the Tests layer below.
:::

Symbols of the notation table (@sec-appa): $\mathcal N_n$, $a_n$, $p$, $p^\circ$, $T$, $\mathcal R$, $g^\circ_n$,
$K^\circ_r$, $\nu_{nr}$, $\xi_r$. Local symbols: $\pi(n)$, the phase of species $n$; $\mathcal N_\pi$, the total
amount of phase $\pi$ [mol]; $r_r$, the residual of reaction $r$ [-]; $\mathsf S$, the stoichiometric matrix with
entries $\nu_{nr}$ (species by reactions); $\mathsf E$, the composition matrix, the number of atoms of element $e$ in
species $n$ (elements by species).

### Derivation

In an ideal mixture the chemical potential of species $n$ is $g^\circ_n + \mathcal R T \ln a_n$, with

$$
\begin{aligned}
a_n &= \frac{\mathcal N_n}{\mathcal N_{\pi(n)}}\,\frac{p}{p^\circ} \quad \text{($n$ in the gas phase)}, \qquad
a_n = \frac{\mathcal N_n}{\mathcal N_{\pi(n)}} \quad \text{(otherwise)}, \\
\mathcal N_\pi &= \sum_{n:\,\pi(n) = \pi} \mathcal N_n .
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch05-conditions-activity}

Reaction $r$ is at equilibrium when the chemical potentials weighted by $\nu_{nr}$ add up to zero:
$\sum_n \nu_{nr} (g^\circ_n + \mathcal R T \ln a_n) = 0$. Dividing by $\mathcal R T$ and moving the standard part to
the right gives one condition per reaction, which the code writes as a residual:

$$
\begin{aligned}
r_r &= \sum_n \nu_{nr} \ln a_n - \ln K^\circ_r = 0 , \\
\ln K^\circ_r &= -\sum_n \nu_{nr}\, \frac{g^\circ_n}{\mathcal R T} .
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch05-conditions-residual}

@eq-ch05-conditions-activity and @eq-ch05-conditions-residual are computed in `equilibrium_max_error`
({{< code src/equilibrium/phase_equilibrate_tp.h equilibrium_max_error >}}): the phase totals, then `log(moles[i] /
phase_totals[phase_ids[i]])` plus `log(pres / standard_pressure)` for the gas, weighted by `stoich` and offset by
`-log_k`.

The unknowns are the reaction extents. Starting from the input amounts $\boldsymbol{\mathcal N}^0$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\boldsymbol{\mathcal N} &= \boldsymbol{\mathcal N}^0 + \mathsf S\,\boldsymbol\xi , \\
\mathsf E\,\boldsymbol{\mathcal N} &= \mathsf E\,\boldsymbol{\mathcal N}^0 + \mathsf E\,\mathsf S\,\boldsymbol\xi
  = \mathsf E\,\boldsymbol{\mathcal N}^0 \quad \text{when } \mathsf E\,\mathsf S = 0 .
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch05-conditions-extent}

$\mathsf E\mathsf S = 0$ says that every reaction is balanced in every element, so any extents conserve the elements
exactly, and the element totals need not be stored. There are as many unknowns as conditions, one per reaction. The
check `newton_check.py` confirms the element balance of a step (`[C2]`), and that for a vapour-liquid pair with
$\ln K^\circ_r = \ln(p^\circ/p_{\mathrm{sat}})$ the condition is Raoult's law, liquid mole fraction times
$p_{\mathrm{sat}}$ equals gas mole fraction times $p$ (`[C4]`).

**A pure condensed phase.** A phase that holds one species has $\mathcal N_\pi = \mathcal N_n$, so
@eq-ch05-conditions-activity gives $a_n = 1$ whatever its amount. Its amount then drops out of every residual, and
the condition of a reaction between gases and that condensate involves only the gas activities. This is the
saturation condition of @sec-ch04-conditions. For example, take $\mathrm{H_2O} \rightleftharpoons
\mathrm{H_2O(l)}$, written towards the liquid as in the check below, with $\ln K^\circ = \ln(p^\circ/p_{\mathrm{sat}})$
and a gas of N$_2$ and water vapour. The residual is

$$
r = \ln 1 - \ln\Big(\frac{\mathcal N_{\mathrm v}}{\mathcal N_{\mathrm v} + \mathcal N_{\mathrm{N_2}}}\,\frac{p}{p^\circ}\Big)
  - \ln\frac{p^\circ}{p_{\mathrm{sat}}}
  = -\ln\frac{\mathcal N_{\mathrm v}\, p}{(\mathcal N_{\mathrm v} + \mathcal N_{\mathrm{N_2}})\, p_{\mathrm{sat}}} ,
$$

and $r = 0$ gives $\mathcal N_{\mathrm v}/(\mathcal N_{\mathrm v} + \mathcal N_{\mathrm{N_2}}) = p_{\mathrm{sat}}/p$,
that is $\mathcal N_{\mathrm v} = \mathcal N_{\mathrm{N_2}}\,p_{\mathrm{sat}}/(p - p_{\mathrm{sat}})$. Unlike
@sec-ch04-conditions, this solver has no complementarity branch: every amount must stay above `mole-floor`, so a phase
that should vanish cannot (@sec-ch05-diagnostics). `check_ch5_equilibrium.py` line a solves this case at 300 K and
$10^5$ Pa, with $p_{\mathrm{sat}}$ from the formula of `h2o_ideal`. The vapour amount matches the closed form to
$2.3\times10^{-12}$ (relative, tolerance $10^{-10}$) after 4 iterations, with status 0, a reported error of
$2.2\times10^{-12}$, and the water total unchanged to the last bit. Line c checks the element balance of
@eq-ch05-conditions-extent on a gas reaction: H and O change by at most $2.2\times10^{-16}$ (relative, tolerance
$10^{-14}$).[^ch05-conditions-check]

### Numerical method

`equilibrium_max_error` ({{< code src/equilibrium/phase_equilibrate_tp.h equilibrium_max_error >}}) evaluates the
residuals of one cell:

1. sum the amounts of each phase;
2. for each species, take the logarithm of its mole fraction within its phase, adding $\ln(p/p^\circ)$ for the gas;
3. accumulate $\nu_{nr}$ times that into each reaction's residual, starting from $-\ln K^\circ_r$;
4. return the largest $|r_r|$, which the Newton iteration of @sec-ch05-newton uses as its convergence measure.

The logarithm needs every amount positive. The solver therefore rejects an input amount that is not above
`mole-floor` (@sec-ch05-diagnostics) and keeps every iterate strictly above it. The conditions hold for every
reaction at once. When the composition at equilibrium has no amount of some phase, as in a subsaturated cell with a
pure liquid, no positive state satisfies them. The iteration then drives that phase to the floor and stops with a
failure status (@sec-ch05-diagnostics). The saturation conditions of @sec-ch04-conditions are inequalities for exactly
this case; these are not.

@fig-ch05-conditions-flash tests the conditions on a two-component ideal solution: gases A and B over a liquid holding
both, with $p_{\mathrm{sat}}$ of 0.4 and 1.6 bar and equal totals, against the closed-form flash. In the 15 cells of
the two-phase window, between 0.65 and 1.0 bar, every solve converges in at most 23 iterations. The liquid fraction
agrees with the closed form to $1.4\times10^{-8}$, and the liquid mole fraction of A to $4.1\times10^{-9}$. In the 22
cells outside the window, where one phase should vanish, every solve stops with status 4 and a reported error between
0.026 and 0.77.[^ch05-flash-run]

### Limits

- **Ideal mixtures only.** Activities are mole fractions within a phase; no activity coefficients, and the gas is
  ideal.
- **No phase can vanish.** Every amount must stay above `mole-floor`; a cell whose equilibrium lacks a phase ends with
  status 4 (@sec-ch05-diagnostics).
- **Condensed activities do not depend on pressure.** Only the gas activities carry $p/p^\circ$.


## Newton iteration in the reaction extents (`phase_equilibrate_tp`) {#sec-ch05-newton}

### Summary

The solver applies Newton's method to the residuals of @sec-ch05-conditions, with the reaction extents as unknowns.
Each iteration builds the exact Jacobian of the residuals with respect to the extents and takes the bounded Newton step
of @sec-ch10-newton, which keeps every amount above `mole-floor`. The step is then halved until the largest residual
decreases. It stops when the largest residual is below the target, or reports why it could not
(@sec-ch05-diagnostics). One cell is solved per thread, on the CPU or on CUDA, and every cell of a batch is
independent.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Solve @eq-ch05-conditions-residual for the extents, @eq-ch05-newton-jacobian.

**Data.** Amounts in and out [mol]; $T$, $p$ and $\ln K^\circ_r$ per cell; gain and diagnostics out.

**Placement.** `EquilibriumTP` forward, per cell, on CPU or CUDA.

**Activation.** Always; YAML `max-iter` (50), `mole-floor` ($10^{-30}$).

**Guarantee / limits.** Amounts stay above the floor and elements are conserved; convergence is not guaranteed.

**Evidence.** See the Tests layer below.
:::

Symbols as in @sec-ch05-conditions. Local symbols: $\mathsf J$, the Jacobian of the residuals with respect to the
extents [mol$^{-1}$]; $\boldsymbol\delta$, the Newton direction in extents [mol]; $\lambda$, the step scale [-];
$\mathcal N_{\mathrm{floor}}$, the value of `mole-floor` [mol]; $\nu_{\pi r} = \sum_{n:\,\pi(n)=\pi} \nu_{nr}$, the
change of phase $\pi$'s total per unit extent of reaction $r$ [-].

### Derivation

With $\boldsymbol{\mathcal N} = \boldsymbol{\mathcal N}^0 + \mathsf S\boldsymbol\xi$, a change of extent $\xi_k$
changes $\mathcal N_n$ by $\nu_{nk}$ and the phase total $\mathcal N_\pi$ by $\nu_{\pi k}$. The pressure factor of the
gas activities is constant. Differentiating @eq-ch05-conditions-residual:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{\partial \ln a_n}{\partial \xi_k} &= \frac{\nu_{nk}}{\mathcal N_n} - \frac{\nu_{\pi(n) k}}{\mathcal N_{\pi(n)}} , \\
\mathsf J_{rk} = \frac{\partial r_r}{\partial \xi_k}
  &= \sum_n \nu_{nr} \Big( \frac{\nu_{nk}}{\mathcal N_n} - \frac{\nu_{\pi(n) k}}{\mathcal N_{\pi(n)}} \Big) .
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch05-newton-jacobian}

`phase_equilibrate_tp` ({{< code src/equilibrium/phase_equilibrate_tp.h phase_equilibrate_tp >}}) builds
`phase_stoich` ($\nu_{\pi k}$) once and then `jac[j * nreaction + k]` exactly as in @eq-ch05-newton-jacobian. The check
`newton_check.py` compares it with central differences of the residual on a three-phase example (`[C1]`), and shows
that a one-species phase contributes nothing: its activity is 1 whatever its amount (`[C3]`). The Newton direction
solves $\mathsf J\boldsymbol\delta = -\mathbf r$. The amounts after a step of scale $\lambda$ must stay above the floor:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal N_n + \lambda \sum_k \nu_{nk}\,\delta_k &> \mathcal N_{\mathrm{floor}} \quad \text{for every } n , \\
-\sum_k \nu_{nk}\,\delta_k &\le \mathcal N_n - \mathcal N_{\mathrm{floor}} .
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch05-newton-bounds}

The second line, at $\lambda = 1$, is the constraint form $\mathsf C\boldsymbol\delta \le \mathbf d$ of
@sec-ch10-newton, with $\mathsf C = -\mathsf S$ and $\mathbf d = \boldsymbol{\mathcal N} - \mathcal N_{\mathrm{floor}}$.
The code sets these rows as `constraints` and `bounds`.

**Why a direct solve.** `constrained_newton_step` factorises $\mathsf J$ itself rather than forming the normal
equations $\mathsf J^{\mathsf T}\mathsf J\boldsymbol\delta = -\mathsf J^{\mathsf T}\mathbf r$. The singular values of
$\mathsf J^{\mathsf T}\mathsf J$ are the squares of those of $\mathsf J$, so the normal equations would square the
condition number. The direct LU solve loses digits in proportion to $\operatorname{cond}(\mathsf J)$ only, which is
the same argument as for the direct form of the constrained least-squares step (@sec-ch04-active-set).

**What the line search guarantees.** Along the Newton direction, a step of scale $\lambda$ changes the residuals by

$$
\mathbf r(\boldsymbol{\mathcal N} + \lambda\mathsf S\boldsymbol\delta) = \mathbf r + \lambda\,\mathsf J\boldsymbol\delta
  + O(\lambda^2) = (1 - \lambda)\,\mathbf r + O(\lambda^2) ,
$$

so every non-zero residual shrinks in proportion, and $\max_r|r_r|$ falls for every small enough $\lambda$. Every
amount is above the floor before the step, so small steps also keep the amounts above it. In exact arithmetic the
halving loop therefore accepts a step whenever the direction is the Newton direction, provided the decrease sets in
above the smallest scale, $10^{-12}$. When the bounds force the
constrained least-squares direction, $\mathsf J\boldsymbol\delta \ne -\mathbf r$, and no decrease is guaranteed. The
loop can then end with status 4. The merit function is the largest residual, and any decrease is accepted. Without
a sufficient-decrease condition, a sequence of accepted steps can stall at a positive error. The vanishing phase of
@sec-ch05-diagnostics is such a case.[^ch05-newton-refs]

### Numerical method

`phase_equilibrate_tp` ({{< code src/equilibrium/phase_equilibrate_tp.h phase_equilibrate_tp >}}) runs these steps in
each cell:

1. **Input checks.** A non-positive temperature or pressure, an empty species or reaction list, a gas phase index out
   of range, or any input amount not above `mole-floor` returns status 1 at once, with the input copied to the output.
2. **Target.** The stop test is $\max_r |r_r| \le \max(\ln(1 + \texttt{ftol}), 4\,\epsilon_{\mathrm{mach}})$; see
   @sec-ch05-diagnostics.
3. **Residuals.** Evaluate @eq-ch05-conditions-residual (@sec-ch05-conditions). If the target is met, stop with
   status 0.
4. **Jacobian.** Build @eq-ch05-newton-jacobian at the current amounts.
5. **Direction.** Call `constrained_newton_step` ({{< code src/math/constrained_newton.h constrained_newton_step >}})
   with the rows of @eq-ch05-newton-bounds. It solves $\mathsf J\boldsymbol\delta = -\mathbf r$ directly and keeps that
   direction unless it leaves a bound with no slack, and only then solves the constrained least-squares problem
   (@sec-ch10-newton, @sec-ch10-kkt), with regularisation $10^{-12}$ and at most `max-iter` inner iterations. A
   failure there stops the solve with status 3.
6. **Line search.** Try $\lambda = 1, \tfrac12, \tfrac14, \dots$ down to $10^{-12}$. A trial is formed by
   `constrained_newton_trial` ({{< code src/math/constrained_newton.h constrained_newton_trial >}}) and accepted when
   every amount is finite and above the floor and the largest residual is smaller than before. If no scale is
   accepted, the solve stops with status 4.
7. **Repeat** from step 3, up to `max-iter` iterations; reaching the cap gives status 2.

The amounts change only by $\mathsf S\lambda\boldsymbol\delta$, so the elements are conserved to round-off
(@eq-ch05-conditions-extent). The per-cell scratch arrays come from a memory pool: on CUDA the driver sizes it with
`equilibrium_space`, including the workspace of the least-squares fallback
(`call_equilibrium_cuda`, {{< code src/equilibrium/equilibrium_dispatch.cu call_equilibrium_cuda >}}). On the CPU the
cells are split over threads by `call_equilibrium_cpu`
({{< code src/equilibrium/equilibrium_dispatch.cpp call_equilibrium_cpu >}}). @fig-ch05-newton-loop gives the order
of the steps.

On a hot H-O gas of six species and four reactions, solved from 2 H$_2$ + O$_2$ with traces of the others at 15
temperatures between 1500 and 5000 K, every solve converges in 11 to 14 iterations. The largest reported error is
$2.0\times10^{-9}$, and H and O are conserved to $4.4\times10^{-16}$ relative. The same runs on CUDA take the same
iteration counts and agree with the CPU to $1.1\times10^{-16}$ in mole fraction.[^ch05-ho-run]

### Limits

- **Convergence is not guaranteed.** The line search only asks that the largest residual decrease; a cell can stop
  with status 4 for reasons other than a vanishing phase. How often that happens on hard systems is not measured.
- **At most 64 components** (`EquilibriumOptionsImpl::validate`), and the reactions must be linearly independent
  (@sec-ch05-options).
- **The constraint rows are fixed at the floor.** A species that should reach zero stays at about the floor and blocks
  convergence (@sec-ch05-diagnostics).

### Summary

`EquilibriumTP` never raises on a cell that does not converge. Each cell returns three numbers: a status code, the
number of Newton steps taken, and the remaining error, the largest relative mismatch between a reaction quotient and
its equilibrium constant. The caller must read them. The forward also returns the Jacobian of the last iteration as a
"gain". The commonest failure on a well-posed problem is a phase that should vanish: the solver cannot remove it and
reports status 4.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Report per cell whether @eq-ch05-conditions-residual was met, @eq-ch05-diagnostics-error.

**Data.** `diagnostics[..., 0:3]` = status, iterations, error; gain, reactions by reactions.

**Placement.** End of `phase_equilibrate_tp`, per cell.

**Activation.** Always; YAML `ftol` ($10^{-8}$).

**Guarantee / limits.** Status 0 means error $\le$ `ftol` in double; nothing is raised or counted.

**Evidence.** See the Tests layer below.
:::

Symbols as in @sec-ch05-conditions and @sec-ch05-newton. Local symbols: $Q_r$, the reaction quotient
$\prod_n a_n^{\nu_{nr}}$ [-]; $\varepsilon$, the reported error [-]; $\epsilon_{\mathrm{mach}}$, the machine epsilon of
the floating type [-].

### Derivation

The residual of @eq-ch05-conditions-residual is $r_r = \ln(Q_r/K^\circ_r)$. The code stops on the largest residual
magnitude and reports it transformed into a relative mismatch:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{stop when } \max_r |r_r| &\le \max\big(\ln(1 + \texttt{ftol}),\ 4\,\epsilon_{\mathrm{mach}}\big) , \\
\varepsilon &= \exp\big(\max_r |r_r|\big) - 1 = \max_r \max\Big(\frac{Q_r}{K^\circ_r}, \frac{K^\circ_r}{Q_r}\Big) - 1 .
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch05-diagnostics-error}

So in double precision status 0 means $\varepsilon \le$ `ftol`: every quotient is within a factor $1 + \texttt{ftol}$ of
its constant. In single precision the floor $4\,\epsilon_{\mathrm{mach}} = 4.8\times10^{-7}$ is larger than the
default `ftol` and sets the target instead (`newton_check.py`, `[C5]`). Both lines are computed in
`phase_equilibrate_tp` ({{< code src/equilibrium/phase_equilibrate_tp.h phase_equilibrate_tp >}}): `target` and
`diag[2] = exp(max_error) - 1`.

### Numerical method

At the end of each cell `phase_equilibrate_tp`
({{< code src/equilibrium/phase_equilibrate_tp.h phase_equilibrate_tp >}}) re-evaluates the residuals at the
returned amounts and writes:

| `diagnostics[..., 0]` | meaning | returned amounts |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | converged: $\max_r |r_r|$ at or below the target | the solution |
| 1 | input rejected: $T$ or $p$ not positive, empty lists, gas phase out of range, or an amount not above `mole-floor` | the input |
| 2 | `max-iter` iterations without meeting the target | the last iterate |
| 3 | the bounded Newton step failed (@sec-ch10-newton) | the last iterate |
| 4 | no step scale down to $10^{-12}$ reduced the largest residual | the last iterate |

: Status codes of the log-K solver. {#tbl-ch05-diagnostics-status}

`diagnostics[..., 1]` is the number of accepted Newton steps: 0 for a cell already at equilibrium or rejected, and
`max-iter` for status 2. `diagnostics[..., 2]` is $\varepsilon$ at the returned amounts, 0 for status 1. The gain is the
Jacobian @eq-ch05-newton-jacobian of the last iteration that built one, evaluated before that iteration's step. It is
all zeros when no iteration built one, that is, for status 1 and for a cell already at equilibrium.
`check_ch5_equilibrium.py` line b evaluates @eq-ch05-newton-jacobian at the converged state of the vapour-liquid
case of @sec-ch05-conditions and matches central differences of the residual to $2.1\times10^{-10}$ (tolerance
$10^{-8}$). The returned gain, 26.28837, differs from that converged-state value, 26.28831, in the seventh significant digit. That
difference is the one-step lag.[^ch05-diagnostics-check]

**A phase that should vanish.** If the equilibrium has no amount of some phase, the iteration drives that phase
towards `mole-floor` and the cell ends with status 4. The mechanism is a hypothesis we have not instrumented: near the
floor the bound of @eq-ch05-newton-bounds caps every step that would reduce the phase further, and for a one-species
phase the residual does not depend on its amount at all (`newton_check.py`, `[C3]`), so no step scale lowers the
largest residual. Its amounts are then close to the one-phase answer, with the phase near the floor, but the error is large:
the reaction that would form the phase is subsaturated. @fig-ch05-diagnostics-water shows this for water vapour over a
pure liquid with NASA-9 constants and a fixed total of water. Up to 300 K the solve converges and the water partial
pressure equals $p^\circ/K^\circ$ to $7.2\times10^{-9}$. From 302.5 K up, where all the water should be vapour,
every cell has status 4, with at most $7.4\times10^{-14}$ mol of liquid left and an error rising from 0.062 to
3.5.[^ch05-water-run]

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- **Nothing is raised or counted.** A cell with a non-zero status keeps its last iterate; the caller must read
  `diagnostics[..., 0]`.
- **A vanishing phase is reported as a failure.** Status 4 does not tell a phase that should vanish from a step that
  stalled for another reason; the caller can tell them apart only by looking at the amounts.
- **The gain lags one step.** It is the Jacobian before the last step, and zero for a cell that needed no step.
:::

- In single precision the target is $4.8\times10^{-7}$, not `ftol`.

### Summary

`EquilibriumOptions` lists the components, the phase of each, the reactions as equation strings, which phase is the
ideal gas, and four numerical options. It can be built field by field through the API or read from a YAML file whose
`phases`, `species`[^rg-065f0144b433] and `reactions` blocks give the same information. The YAML reader also checks that every reaction
conserves every element. The API path cannot, because it carries no compositions. Building `EquilibriumTP` from the
options forms the stoichiometric matrix and refuses linearly dependent reactions.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Define the system of @eq-ch05-conditions-residual and the options of @sec-ch05-newton.

**Data.** Components, phases, phase of each component, reaction equations; four numerical options.

**Placement.** Before the first solve; `EquilibriumTP` reads the options when it is built.

**Activation.** `EquilibriumOptions.from_yaml(path)` or the API setters.

**Guarantee / limits.** Element balance is checked only by the YAML reader; at most 64 components.

**Evidence.** See the Tests layer below.
:::

Symbols as in @sec-ch05-conditions.

### Derivation

No derivation: this scheme maps an input to the matrices $\mathsf S$ and $\mathsf E$ and the phase map $\pi(n)$ of
@sec-ch05-conditions.

### Numerical method

`EquilibriumOptionsImpl::from_yaml`
({{< code src/equilibrium/equilibrium_options.cpp EquilibriumOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}) reads the file in order:

1. **Phases.** Each entry of `phases` has a name and a list of species, which become the components in the order
   listed. The phase whose `thermo` (or `type`[^rg-9292dca86f77]) is `ideal-gas` is the gas phase. Exactly one phase must be, and a
   component may belong to only one phase. Any other `thermo` value makes a condensed ideal mixture.
2. **Species.** Each entry of `species` has a name and a `composition`[^rg-54a1072b5f2c] map. Every component must have one, and a
   species defined twice is refused. The elements are the union of the composition keys.
3. **Reactions.** Each entry of `reactions` with no `type`, or with `type: equilibrium`, is kept; every other type is
   skipped, so a file can also hold the kinetics of @sec-ch06. Every kept reaction must name only components and must
   balance every element to $10^{-10}$; otherwise the reader raises "does not conserve element".
4. **Numerical options.** An optional `equilibrium` block sets the four values below.
5. **Validation.** The options must have non-empty lists, one phase index per component and in range, at most 64
   components, a gas phase in range, positive standard pressure, `max-iter` and `ftol`, and a non-negative
   `mole-floor`.
   They are made by the validation function of the code map below.

| key | meaning | default | read by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `standard-pressure` | $p^\circ$ of @eq-ch05-conditions-activity [Pa] | $10^5$ | `from_yaml` |
| `max-iter` | Newton iterations, also the inner bound of the least-squares fallback | 50 | `from_yaml` |
| `ftol` | relative tolerance of @eq-ch05-diagnostics-error | $10^{-8}$ | `from_yaml` |
| `mole-floor` | lower bound on every amount [mol] | $10^{-30}$ | `from_yaml` |

: Keys of the `equilibrium` block. {#tbl-ch05-options-keys}

The same defaults apply when the block is absent or the options are built through the API
(`EquilibriumOptionsImpl`, {{< code src/equilibrium/equilibrium.hpp EquilibriumOptionsImpl >}}). Building
`EquilibriumTP` runs `EquilibriumTPImpl::reset`
({{< code src/equilibrium/equilibrium.cpp EquilibriumTPImpl::reset >}}), which validates again, forms the
stoichiometric matrix from the equation strings in component order, and refuses it unless its rank equals the number
of reactions. A reaction that is a combination of others would make the Jacobian of @sec-ch05-newton singular.
@fig-ch05-options-path follows a YAML file to the solver.

::: {.cell execution_count=5}

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5}
![From a YAML input to the buffers of EquilibriumTP. Boxes in reading order; grey notes give the checks made at each stage.](05-chemical-equilibrium_files/figure-pdf/fig-ch05-options-path-output-1.pdf){#fig-ch05-options-path fig-alt='Five boxes left to right: phases, species, reactions, validate, EquilibriumTP; notes under them: one ideal-gas phase, each reaction balanced in every element, at most 64 components, reactions independent.'}

The kintera example `examples/equilibrium_nasa9.yaml` is such a file: one `ideal-gas` phase with H$_2$, O$_2$ and
H$_2$O, the reaction H$_2$ + ½ O$_2$ $\rightleftharpoons$ H$_2$O, and an `equilibrium` block with `max-iter: 100`. The runs of this chapter
use small inputs of the same form written by `run_equilibrium.py`. The two-phase ones give a second phase with

## Equilibrium constants from NASA-9 polynomials (`Nasa9LogK`) {#sec-ch05-log-k}

### Summary

The solver takes $\ln K^\circ_r$ as an input. `Nasa9LogK` computes it from the NASA-9 polynomials bundled with
kintera: it evaluates each component's $g^\circ_n/\mathcal R T$ and contracts it with the stoichiometric matrix of the
options. The data file, described in @sec-ch02-nasa9, holds 293 species with two temperature ranges, 200 to 1000 K
and 1000 to 6000 K. Besides
gases it has a few condensed entries, such as liquid and solid water, which a component can be mapped to by name. The
constants are those at the standard pressure; the pressure of a cell enters only through the gas activities.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** $\ln K^\circ_r$ of @eq-ch05-conditions-residual from tabulated data, @eq-ch05-log-k-gibbs.

**Data.** $T$ [K] in, any shape; $\ln K^\circ_r$ out, shape `(..., R)` in option reaction order.

**Placement.** Python, before each solve; any device.

**Activation.** `Nasa9LogK(options, nasa9_species=None)`; names default to the components.

**Guarantee / limits.** Two ranges joined at 1000 K; no range check; the pressure argument is ignored.

**Evidence.** See the Tests layer below.
:::

Symbols as in @sec-ch05-conditions; $h_n$ and $s_n$ of the notation table, here at $p^\circ$. Local symbols:
$c_{p,n}$, the heat capacity at constant pressure of species $n$ [J mol$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$]; $\Delta_r h^\circ =
\sum_n \nu_{nr} h_n$, the standard reaction enthalpy [J mol$^{-1}$].

### Derivation

The NASA-9 forms of $h_n/\mathcal R T$ and $s_n/\mathcal R$ in each range are @eq-ch02-nasa9-forms
(@sec-ch02-nasa9). The Gibbs energy and the constant follow:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{g^\circ_n}{\mathcal R T} &= \frac{h_n}{\mathcal R T} - \frac{s_n}{\mathcal R} , \\
\ln K^\circ_r &= -\sum_n \nu_{nr}\, \frac{g^\circ_n}{\mathcal R T} .
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch05-log-k-gibbs}

The first line is `nasa9_gibbs_RT` ({{< code src/thermo/nasa9.hpp nasa9_gibbs_RT >}}), which takes the low
coefficients below the mid-point temperature and the high ones above it. The second line is `Nasa9LogK.__call__`
({{< code python/equilibrium/nasa9.py Nasa9LogK >}}), `-(gibbs_rt @ stoich)`, with the `stoich` buffer of an
`EquilibriumTP` built from the same options.

**Why this is the constant.** Three steps connect @eq-ch05-log-k-gibbs to the conditions of @sec-ch05-conditions.

1. At equilibrium the chemical potentials $\mu_n = g^\circ_n + \mathcal R T\ln a_n$, weighted by $\nu_{nr}$, add up to
   zero. Dividing by $\mathcal R T$ gives $\sum_n \nu_{nr}\ln a_n = -\sum_n \nu_{nr} g^\circ_n/(\mathcal R T)$, and the
   right side is $\ln K^\circ_r$ of @eq-ch05-log-k-gibbs.
2. The standard state of a gas is the pure ideal gas at $p^\circ$, and that of a condensed species is the pure phase.
   So $g^\circ_n$ depends on $T$ only, and the pressure enters only through the gas activities $x_n p/p^\circ$ of
   @eq-ch05-conditions-activity. $K^\circ_r$ is dimensionless and independent of $p$. A reaction that changes the
   number of gas molecules responds to pressure through the factor $(p/p^\circ)^{\sum_{n\,\in\,\mathrm{gas}} \nu_{nr}}$
   of its quotient.
3. The temperature derivative follows from the forms of $h_n$ and $s_n$. At fixed $p^\circ$, $\mathrm dh_n/\mathrm dT =
   c_{p,n}$ and $\mathrm ds_n/\mathrm dT = c_{p,n}/T$, so

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dT}\frac{h_n}{\mathcal R T} &= \frac{c_{p,n}}{\mathcal R T} - \frac{h_n}{\mathcal R T^2} , \qquad
\frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dT}\frac{s_n}{\mathcal R} = \frac{c_{p,n}}{\mathcal R T} , \qquad
\frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dT}\frac{g^\circ_n}{\mathcal R T} = -\frac{h_n}{\mathcal R T^2} , \\
\frac{\mathrm d\ln K^\circ_r}{\mathrm dT} &= -\sum_n \nu_{nr}\,\frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dT}\frac{g^\circ_n}{\mathcal R T}
  = \frac{\sum_n \nu_{nr}\, h_n}{\mathcal R T^2} = \frac{\Delta_r h^\circ}{\mathcal R T^2} .
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch05-log-k-vant-hoff}

The third relation of the first line is the Gibbs–Helmholtz equation, and the second line is the van 't Hoff
equation:[^ch05-logk-refs] an exothermic reaction ($\Delta_r h^\circ < 0$) has a constant that falls with temperature.
Within one NASA-9 range the identity holds exactly for the polynomial forms of @eq-ch02-nasa9-forms, because they are
the integrals of one $c_{p,n}$ polynomial. At the mid-point temperature the coefficient set changes. Whether $h_n$
and $s_n$ are continuous there is a property of the data, not something the code enforces (@sec-ch02-nasa9). The
temperature derivative of reverse rate constants (@sec-ch06-mass-action) rests on the same identity.

`check_ch5_equilibrium.py` line c solves 2 H$_2$ + O$_2$ $\rightleftharpoons$ 2 H$_2$O at 3500 K and $p = p^\circ$ with
`Nasa9LogK`. Its own parse of the bundled table reproduces the library's $\Delta_r g^\circ/(\mathcal R T)$ exactly. The
derivative of $\ln K^\circ$ by central differences matches $\Delta_r h^\circ/(\mathcal R T^2)$ from the integrated
enthalpy to $4.7\times10^{-10}$ (tolerance $10^{-6}$). The solved state meets its residual to $8.0\times10^{-12}$
(tolerance $10^{-10}$), with H and O conserved to $2.2\times10^{-16}$.[^ch05-logk-check]

### Numerical method

1. **Construction.** `Nasa9LogK(options, nasa9_species)` keeps one NASA-9 name per component, by default the
   component names, and the stoichiometric matrix of the options.
2. **Data.** `nasa9_gibbs_rt` ({{< code src/species.cpp nasa9_gibbs_rt >}}) reads `data/nasa9.dat` once per process,
   guarded so that concurrent first calls are safe. It looks up each name, raising "NASA-9 species not found" for an
   unknown one, and calls `nasa9_gibbs_RT` with a mid-point of 1000 K for every species.
3. **Evaluation.** `__call__(temp, pressure)` returns $\ln K^\circ_r$ on the device and dtype of `temp`. The pressure
   argument is deleted unused.

For an ideal gas the constants are those at $p^\circ$, and the cell pressure enters through the factor $p/p^\circ$ of
@eq-ch05-conditions-activity, so ignoring the argument is correct there. For a condensed species it means the
constant has no pressure correction (@sec-ch05-conditions, Limits).

**A condensed species from the same file.** Mapping the liquid of the water card of @sec-ch05-diagnostics to the
entry `H2O_l_s` gives, for H$_2$O $\rightleftharpoons$ H$_2$O(l), a saturation pressure $p^\circ/K^\circ$ of 3533.6 Pa at 300 K. kintera's
own liquid-water curve `h2o_ideal` gives 3539.5 Pa there, so the two sources differ by $1.7\times10^{-3}$
relative.[^ch05-logk-water] @fig-ch05-log-k-gas shows the constants and the equilibrium they give for a hot H-O gas.
Above about 3500 K atomic H and the radical OH take over from water (at 3500 K, $x_{\mathrm{H_2O}} = 0.231$,
$x_{\mathrm{OH}} = 0.157$, $x_{\mathrm{H}} = 0.253$).[^ch05-logk-ho]

### Limits

- **No range check.** Temperatures below 200 K or above 6000 K are evaluated with the low or high coefficients
  without a warning; the accuracy there is not measured.
- **One mid-point for all species.** The coefficients switch at 1000 K for every species, as the file's two ranges
  are stated.
- **The pressure argument is ignored**, which is right for ideal gases and leaves condensed constants without a
  pressure correction.
